phase1_acceptance.retention_rule: Before a checkpoint can become unreachable, retain its exact bytes under a deterministic content-addressed role-local path in the current reachable namespace and record source snapshot/checkpoint identity plus digest in the current manifest.
phase1_acceptance.retry_rule: On ambiguous retention create response, read the deterministic path and verify exact digest before retry; never allocate a fresh retention identity blindly.
phase1_acceptance.recovery_rule: Prefer verified current-reachable retained bytes; fall back to the historical SHA only if fetchable. Never substitute same-path or mutable-ref-name content without exact identity.
phase1_acceptance.authority_rule: After bytes are reconstructed, revalidate current semantic authority before selecting/updating LATEST.
phase1_acceptance.gc_rule: Application GC may delete a retained copy only after the current role-local manifest no longer marks that snapshot/checkpoint identity as a recovery root; missing expected content before then is a blocker, not evidence of safe absence.
phase1_acceptance.retention_scope_caveat: No claim that GitHub.com retains unreachable historical objects indefinitely or that an unprotected mutable ref is permanent.
phase1_acceptance.inherited_open_boundary: Complete repository rollback that removes both retained copy and current manifest remains unresolved; fail closed rather than resurrect old authority.
